sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties.

2. This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:-
"For issuance a writ or writs, direction or directions, commanding upon the respondents to reassess the valuation of their land, building and trees situated and standing in Mouza Kaswa, Arajimokimpur under Thana no.27 and 26, plot no.808,
807 and plot no.6 and pay them compensation after reassessing and re-evaluating the same at market rate which is four times higher than the agriculture land etc. as the landed property are situated in the market area where the house of the petitioners with some commercial complex are standing.

A direction may also be given upon the respondents authority to either reassess the valuation of the land or to send it to the appropriate authority for proper reassessment and determination of Award in terms of Sections 26 to 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013."
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners has referred to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and has submitted that assessment with regard to the value of the land and property involved in the present case has been done in violation of the provisions of Section 29 and 94 of the said Act.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He has submitted that the land has been acquired for the purposes of National Highway but the compensation is payable in terms of the aforesaid Act of 2013.
The respondents having not done the valuation properly.
The facts mentioned in the writ petition with regard to the property involved in this writ petition have not been disputed by the respondents.
4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the National Highway has submitted that some amount of compensation has been offered to the petitioners.
They can accept the amount under protest and can still get the matter regarding quantum of compensation decided in terms of Section 3G (5) of the National Highway Act, 1956.
5. She has submitted that the quantum of compensation has to be fixed in terms of the provisions of the Act.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, it appears that there is a dispute with regard to the amount of compensation that the petitioners are entitled.
It further appears that the petitioners have been offered certain compensation but they have neither received it nor they have agitated their grievance in terms of section 3G (5) of the Act.

8. So far as the offered amount to the petitioners is concerned, they may accept the same under protest but certainly the amount is to be disbursed after due identification and in accordance with law .
9. This writ petition is accordingly disposed of.
